case_title: Pradeep Kumar v. State of Haryana
accused_victim_relationship: Not stated (only alleged: co-accused A-2 borrowed money from the deceased; not relied on by the Court)
weapon: Dandas (sticks); no sharp-edged weapon recovered, though the doctor attributed an incise wound to a sharp-edged weapon
evidence_type: Circumstantial (no eyewitnesses); also medical post-mortem evidence, recoveries, forensic (FSL) blood-group report, alleged extra-judicial confession, and last-seen witnesses
confession: Alleged extra-judicial confession made to village Sarpanch (PW-10); the Supreme Court rejected the Sarpanch as not trustworthy and did not rely on it
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under s.302 read with s.34 IPC for murder; sentenced to rigorous imprisonment for life
high_court_outcome: Appeal dismissed; conviction and life sentence confirmed
neutral_facts: On the evening of 10 April 2004 the victim left a workplace on his motorcycle after receiving two phone calls, saying he had to go to a market. The next morning his family reported him missing. His body was later found lying in a field with his throat tied with cloth, one eye badly injured and injuries to the head. The post-mortem doctor found an incised wound that, in the doctor's view, was caused by a sharp-edged weapon. Investigators recorded statements from several persons. One witness said he saw four young men on a motorcycle carrying sticks near a bypass that evening, one of them with blood-stained clothing, and noted a registration number. Another said he saw three young men on a motorcycle holding sticks at a road junction around 10 pm and recognised one of them. A third said he saw the victim seated on a motorcycle with one of the accused at a junction. After a surrender, the accused were said to have made an extra-judicial confession before a village sarpanch, who also said he had seen the victim earlier that evening. Police recovered sticks, a pair of trousers and a mobile phone. Forensic tests reported blood of the same group as the victim on the sticks and trousers. No sharp-edged weapon was recovered. The recoveries were not made in the presence of any independent witness. The case rested entirely on circumstantial evidence, with no eyewitness to the killing.
physical_harm: Death of the victim; throat tied with cloth, badly injured right eye, injuries on the head, and an incise wound attributed to a sharp-edged weapon
premeditation_planning: Not identified by the Court; the alleged planning, described in the extra-judicial confession account, was not accepted
motive: alleged: co-accused's loan from the deceased and pressure to repay it; not accepted by the Court
key_evidence_accepted: No evidence was accepted as establishing guilt. The Court noted the post-mortem incise wound and the FSL blood-group match (O+) but held the match was not an indication of guilt
witness_credibility: PW-10 (Sarpanch) not trustworthy; PW-11 (chance witness) completely unreliable; PW-12 (chance witness) does not inspire confidence; PW-16 (relative) version highly improbable and unreliable; IO's recoveries lacked independent witnesses
post_offence_conduct: Alleged surrender on 17.04.2004 through the village Sarpanch with an alleged extra-judicial confession; the Court found the confession false and unbelievable
trial_duration: offence: 10.04.2004; trial judgment: 31.08.2007; High Court: 05.09.2009; Supreme Court: 05.01.2024
legal_representation: Appellant: Pranab Kumar Mullick, Mrs. Soma Mullick and others (Advocates). State: Ajay Bansal, A.A.G., Gaurav Yadava and others (Advocates)
investigation_status: FIR registered; investigation completed; charge sheet filed; trial completed
procedural_irregularity: Recoveries made without any independent witness; IO admitted not trying to join a private person; High Court relied on PW-11 and PW-12 without discussing PW-10
appeal_history: Trial Court: convicted under s.302 r/w s.34 IPC, life imprisonment. High Court: appeal dismissed, conviction and sentence confirmed. Supreme Court: appeal allowed, accused acquitted
defence_argument: Weapons recovered and seen were only sticks, while the fatal incise wound indicates a sharp-edged weapon; the witnesses' versions are contradictory and improbable; the FSL trouser description does not match the recovered jeans; the blood-group match is not indicative of guilt; recoveries lacked independent witnesses
legal_principle_applied: Circumstantial evidence test: circumstances must be fully established, consistent only with guilt, exclude every other hypothesis, and form a complete chain; suspicion cannot replace proof beyond reasonable doubt
precedent_relied_upon: Pritinder Singh v. State of Punjab, (2023) 7 SCC 727; Sharad Birdhichand Sarda v. State of Maharashtra, (1984) 4 SCC 116
other_sentence_order: Bail bonds discharged; pending applications disposed of; parties to bear their own costs
